mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown a consistent, albeit slowing, upward trend over the past four weeks, indicating a gradual return to pre-pandemic activity levels. This underlying momentum suggests continued recovery in retail and recreation mobility.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, indicating a reversal of the observed recovery trend.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp drop in PARKS mobility in the most recent week suggests a shift in outdoor leisure patterns, possibly due to changing weather or the end of peak summer outdoor activity. This reallocation of leisure time will redirect some activity towards indoor retail and recreation.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by more than 15 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase, or decreases, in the two weeks following a significant PARKS mobility drop.

mechanism_narrative: The slight uptick in RESIDENTIAL mobility at t-0w, combined with the slowing recovery of RETAIL_REC, suggests a plateauing of out-of-home activity. If people spend more time at home, they will spend less in retail and recreation, leading to a decline.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL increases while RETAIL_REC increase slows
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues its upward trend despite the increase in RESIDENTIAL mobility and slowing RETAIL_REC recovery.

mechanism_narrative: The recent decline in GROCERY_PHARM mobility indicates reduced essential shopping trips, which often correlates with a general reduction in out-of-home activity. This suggests a broader trend of caution or reduced movement, negatively impacting discretionary retail and recreation.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases in the week following a two-week decline in GROCERY_PHARM mobility.

mechanism_narrative: Despite a slight dip at t-0w, TRANSIT mobility has shown a general upward trend over the last three weeks. If this recovery resumes and TRANSIT mobility rises above -53%, it signals increased commuting and general movement, which will positively impact retail and recreation.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase even if TRANSIT mobility rises above -53% from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: The stagnation of WORKPLACES mobility, combined with persistently low TRANSIT usage, indicates that a significant return to office-based work is not occurring. This lack of weekday footfall will continue to suppress RETAIL_REC, particularly for businesses reliant on office workers.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -45% and TRANSIT remains below -50%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC shows a significant increase despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility remaining low.

mechanism_narrative: The overall trend of RESIDENTIAL mobility decreasing (less time at home) over the past few weeks, despite a small recent uptick, suggests a continued gradual shift towards out-of-home activities. This sustained behavioral change will eventually translate to higher RETAIL_REC.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility increases significantly, or RETAIL_REC declines, over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The significant drop in PARKS mobility at t-0w, likely due to seasonal changes or the conclusion of summer holidays, will cause a reallocation of leisure time and spending from outdoor activities to indoor retail and recreation, boosting RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility drops by more than 20 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the week following a sharp decline in PARKS mobility.
